speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise during your pregnancy. To help me pinpoint the cause, how many weeks pregnant are you, and when did these symptoms first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old female at 30 weeks gestation. The patient presents with a sudden onset of fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. She reports the consumption of ice cream 3 days prior to the onset of symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the information. Consuming ice cream shortly before the onset of fever, headache, and anorexia is concerning; do you recall if the dairy was unpasteurized or if the container was bulging? REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture, Complete_Blood_Count, Liver_Function_Tests.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Listeriosis (Listeria monocytogenes infection). The clinical picture of a 30-week pregnant patient presenting with fever, headache, anorexia, and malaise shortly after consuming ice cream is highly suggestive of this condition, often associated with unpasteurized dairy. The requested tests (Blood Culture, CBC, LFTs) and serologies would confirm the diagnosis.
